                                     Principal’s Message

                              From the Desk of the Principal:
      Heartiest Greetings from the entire family of Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College, Guwahati...

                                        नहिज्ञाने नसदृशं पहित्रहमिहिदयते ।
                                 तत्स्वयंयोगसां हसद्धः कालेनात्महनहिन्दहत॥ (4.38)

        Knowledge provides a clear vision, we must consistently strive to realize that knowledge to
achieve perfection, says the Bhagavad Gita. ‘Colleges’ are the modern forms of Gurugrihas. Both from the
ancient and modern definitions; and the philosophies from the East and the West, it is beautifully reflected
that Colleges, the other name of Higher Educational Institutes are the Power Houses, created by the
Human Resources and for the Great going of the Nation and the World for peace and development.
Therefore, it is popularly said that ….’No Knowledge, without College’.

        Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College shortly KHSC, a seat of Higher learning was established by a
group of philanthropists in 1988 with a view to disseminating skill, knowledge and wisdom among the
youths, who were compelled to live in the city for job engagements but adversely suffered from lack of
higher education. For benefitting the city dwellers through proper arrangements of higher education, this
college was established in the outgrowths of Guwahati city. Therefore, originally the college was known as
City College. After few years of establishment, with a view to showing the ‘Respect’ to former Chief
Minister of Assam, Honourable Hiteswar Saikia, for his unparallel services in the field of Higher Education
under the greater educational reforms in public sector education in the state of Assam, this college was
named as Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College. The nomenclature signifies the motto ‘work is
worship’...KARMASHREE and the beautiful inundation of young hearts and minds decode the spirited
workforce for a holistic development in the field of higher education.

        Our college, KHSC, comprises of two streams with 10 departments and a beautiful as well as
gainful mixture of a few jobs guaranteed ADD ON Courses. The beautiful campus, the well-skilled and
knowledgeable faculties, a resourceful library and a strong community linkage of our college can distinctly
highlight in the educational map of Higher Education of Assam. The entire College family is ready to accept
any type of challenges of higher education under NEP2020.

        The college authority is ready to take its utmost care in each and every aspect of student-centric
education. For us the interpersonal capabilities of the students are more important than their percentage
of marks in examinations. The authority promises a 360 degree and 24x7 CARE for the betterment of the
students. The College shall try to ignite the positivity through PMA (Positive Mental Attitude) among the
students and to inculcate the dynamism to keep pace with the present World. Along with the Academic all
the other extra-curricular talents are also taken care passionately for plucking the fruits. Our institution
will upraise the work-culture and inculcate the intensive care for generating the multidimensional
capabilities of the students. Though the facilities and hands are limited yet we thrive to invest our best
and entire force through a whole-hearted approach to flourish the talents of the students.

The best definition of the best college does not admit the exhibitionism, external beauty and
exaggerations. The best college is not defined by rankings, not even by her physical features like buildings
                             Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College | Prospectus 2026–27
 or playgrounds; but the best college is found in her high return or investment, strong Career
concentration, skill generation as well as up gradation, supportive environment, value outcomes, mutual
respects and honour for a holistic living and working. Our college is always ready to uphold all these
features connotatively aiming the motto of Peace and Development. World famous poet W.B. Yeats
rightfully characterized education as “the lighting of a fire,” rather than “the filling of a pail,”
emphasizing the nurturing of imagination, character, and passion over rote memorization or mere
accumulation of facts. His view favoured fostering creative, independent thought and the development of
the whole person. The forces of education are enough for changing and shaping the Human Civilization.
Really it is hard time to remember that definition and to accept the growing challenges of education in
general and higher education in particular for changing the World with full of confidence and selfness.

        The aim of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s vision of education is to spread enlightened idea among the people
for the reconstruction of the society on the principles of liberty, equality, fraternity and justice. According
to Ambedkar – “Education is a weapon of creation of mental and educational development, weapon of
eradication of social slavery of economic development of political freedom”. Again, he remarked
“Education is what makes a person fearless, teaches him the lesson of unity, makes him aware of rights
and inspires him to struggle for his rights.” It beautifully reveals that education is nothing but an untiring
movement for freedom.

       Dear Friends, it is a hard era with soft technology. Policy of Higher Education has been changed
purposively. NEP 2020 reflects the pros and cons of India’s education system and welcomes for a dignified
Educational Environment so that the transparency, adaptability, skill generative technology-based
education and dynamism and creativity can confidently overcome the obstacles so that our education
system is incarnated as the ‘VISWAGURU’

         Dear Friends, we the KHS College do sincerely promise to provide the best for overall qualitative
improvement of our College. Our journey is purely student-centric and for us each and every student is
unique and unparallel. We try to focus on diversified capabilities and qualities of the students along with
critical thinking ability, not on percentage of marks alone. Because we strongly believe that percentage of
marks fail to recognize the success but skill and capability do can.

        Anyway, we do sincerely believe that in the nearest future, our college will be placed in the midst
of the brightness of Assam’s higher education map. So, we, the College family do sincerely believe in the
motto … ‘Unity is our Strength’. I, as the Principal of the College do appeal to the Government to extend
their kindness to have a ‘Beautiful Jerk’ in our Great Institution with the Holistic Mission of ‘Work for
Change and Development’.

 About the College
Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College

       Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College is one of the prominent institutions of higher education in
Assam, known for its commitment to academic excellence and social development. Since its establishment
in 1988, the college has been playing a vital role in imparting quality education to students, especially
those from diverse socio-economic backgrounds. Situated at Six Mile, Guwahati, the college offers a
peaceful and conducive environment for learning and intellectual development of the students coming
from the different parts of the state and Northeast India.

The College Traversing the Course of Time:

        With the shifting of the capital of Assam from Shillong to Dispur in 1973, the city of Guwahati
witnessed rapid population growth and urban expansion. However, facilities for higher education
remained limited, as the existing colleges in the city were unable to accommodate the increasing number
of students. As a result, many aspiring learners were deprived of opportunities for higher education.

        Recognizing this gap and understanding the urgency of the situation, a group of prominent
educationists and social activists envisioned the establishment of a new college in the south-eastern part
of Guwahati, near the Assam–Meghalaya inter-state border. Their efforts led to the founding of
Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College, originally established as City College on 19thSeptember, 1988 at the
O.B.C. Complex, Dispur. This initiative was spearheaded by late Tholok Gogoi, whose vision was to impart
higher education to the downtrodden and underprivileged sections of society.

       Late Tholok Gogoi, the founder secretary of the college, was also the General Secretary of the All
Assam Other Backwards Classes Association, the “Mantri” of the Assam Rastrabhasha Prachar Samiti, and
a dedicated social worker throughout his life. His untiring efforts and commitment to social upliftment
played a crucial role in shaping the institution and its mission.

         The early years of City College, the dream project of Tholok Gogoi, were marked by severe
financial constraints and lack of basic infrastructure. Despite these challenges, the college managed to
survive until 1992 without its own land or buildings. A turning point came with the support of Hiteswar
Saikia, the then Chief Minister of Assam. Recognizing the need for a higher educational institution in the


                             Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College | Prospectus 2026–27
 south-eastern part of Guwahati, he allotted land at Sixmile, Panjabari Road, during his tenure. The college
was subsequently shifted to this new campus on 29thFebruary 1996- the present site of the college.

        A new Governing Body was later constituted under the presidentship of Dr. Hemoprava Saikia.
Under her dynamic leadership, the institution progressed steadily. In recognition of the immense
contribution of Hiteswar Saikia, the college was officially renamed as Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College
on 4thJanuary 2004 at a public meeting attended by eminent citizens, educationists, and students of the
state.

       Initially, the college offered both Higher Secondary and undergraduate (B.A.) courses. However, in
2000, the Higher Secondary section was separated and shifted to the Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia
Secondary School.

       Over the years, the college has witnessed steady infrastructuredevelopment. The Uma Charan
Bania Memorial Library and Education Centre was established on 8thJanuary 2011 through the generous
support of the family of Late Uma Charan Bania. A centrally air-conditioned auditoriumwas inaugurated
on 6th May 2016 with assistance from the Government of Assam. On 9thFebruary 2019, Kumud Ch. Deka
Memorial open stage was donated by the family of Late Kumud Chandra Deka.

        It received permanent affiliation from Gauhati University in 2010 for its Arts stream. It was
recognized under Sections 2(f) and 12(B) of the UGC Act, 1956 in 2013, and its Arts stream was
provincialized in 2013 by the Government of Assam. Besides, adding another feather to its cap the college
started the Commerce streamin 2013 in self-financed mode.

The college also got the first ever NAAC Accreditation in 2022 securing Grade B.

The College Today:

       Today, the college stands as a growing co-educational institution offering Arts and Commerce
courses in a serene academic environment. It runs anarray of undergraduate courses in Arts and
Commerce. In addition to traditional courses, the college also provides professional and skill-based
programmes, cultural and sports facilities for the students. The college has an active NSS (National Service
Scheme) unit, a moral and spiritual study centre, different hobby clubs, add on course like Montessori
Training Centre, and Tailoring Course. Besides, to facilitate its academic endeavour the college has a
KKHSOU study centre that runs both undergraduate and post graduate courses.

        The infrastructure of the college supports its academic mission. It has well-equipped classrooms
with digital facilities, a digitalized library with a rich collection of books and journals, and an auditorium
and open stage for cultural and academic activities. The college also organizes a good number of national
and international seminars, conference, lectures, workshops, etc. for enriching its academic contribution
and uplifting the students, teachers and the community. These activities help in the holistic development
of studentsby nurturing their talents and building confidence.

        An important aspect of the college is its dedication to social responsibility. It has an adopted
village named Nam-tepesia in Sonapur locality. The college promotes awareness about environmental
issues, social harmony, and community service. Through various initiatives, students are encouraged to
engage with society and contribute positively to the community. This reflects the broader vision of
education as not just the acquisition of knowledge, but also the development of responsible citizens.

                              Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College | Prospectus 2026–27
         Karmashree Hiteswar Saikia College stands as a symbol of educational progress in Assam. With its
dedication to quality education, inclusive growth, and student development, the college continues to
shape the future of countless young minds. It remains an important centre of learning, contributing not
only to academic advancement but also to the social and cultural enrichment of the region.

        The collegehas been able to carve a niche in the academic ground with its sustained academic
engagement, vibrant co-curricular activities, and meaningful outreach initiatives. The faculty members
have been ceaselessly striving towardsaccomplishing their commitment to quality teaching, research, and
mentoring, while the students actively participate in academic, cultural, and extension activities, bringing
laurels to the college.


       The names of the philanthropists like Uma Konwar, Pradip Saikia, Atul Buragohain, etc. were so
genuinely associated in the architecture of the college that the strength of the institution became
unparalleled at this time.

        In this entire period of educational journey, the college was headed by Chambus Gogoi, Dr. Arun
Barua, Dr. Ramesh Buragohain, Ananda Buragohain, and Dr. Sikhamoni Konwar and very recently Dr.
Budhen Kumar Saikia as Principal of this great seat of higher learning. In 2026, with the inclusion of 15
numbers of skill development courses from Psychological Health to Artificial Intelligence, the college has
started a beautiful big jerk for a skillful student-centric growth strategy to stand before the challenging
world. To flourish the innate talents of each and every student is also an innovative challenging approach
for greater going of the institution.

In this entire ‘Holistic’ journey , the motto of “Think Global and Act Local” paves the way for facing the
challenges of higher education at this present time.

fine of Rs. 2.00 shall be levied per day for 15 days, and thereafter Rs. 5.00 per day till the date of return.

                                       STUDENTS UNION
The College Students’ Union is the general body consisting the students of the college. Its membership is
compulsory for every student. The office bearers of the Union body are elected annually.

                   COLLEGE RULES AND REGULATIONS
1. The college lays great emphasis on discipline and character building of the students. A student, if found
guilty of disobeying college rules, will have to face strict disciplinary action, which includes expulsion from
the college/rusticated for a period/debarred from appearing in any examination for one or more years
etc. Such disciplinary action will be decided by the * Disciplinary Committee * headed by Principal, and
her decision shall be final in all such matters.

2. All forms of ragging in the college campus are strictly prohibited. Anyone found indulging in ragging will
be firmly dealt with disciplinary action.

3. Any violation of college rules, unsatisfactory progress, irregular attendance, non-clearance of college
dues, discourtesy to faculty members in any form, or adoption of unfair means during examination will be
dealt with strictly.

4. Any notice desired to be put up or circulated to students on the college campus will require the prior
approval of the college authority.

5. Use of mobile phones in the classrooms is strictly prohibited.

6. Students who fail to attend 75% of total classes held in an academic year are not allowed to appear in
any examination. This applies to all the subjects, both Major & Minor.

7. Students must attend all the sessional examinations, failing which he/she shall not be allowed to appear
in G.U. Final Examination.

8. Students, along with their Parents/guardians, are requested to be present in the Orientation Day that is
to be observed on the 1st day of the new session.

9. The course of study in the college is based as a full-time course. So, no student is allowed to pursue any
other course of study simultaneously in another institution.

10. The college is a tobacco-free zone. Use of tobacco in the college premises is strictly prohibited.

11. The college is a plastic-free and environmentally viable zone. Use of plastic in the college premises is
strictly prohibited.



                                       IDENTITY CARDS
A non-transferable Identity Card will be issued to every student at the time of admission. The students are
required to keep the identity cards with them during college hours and have to be produced whenever
demanded. Identity cards are issued annually.
